subject: Communication
title: EQ in Relationships: Gottman's Discoveries
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: EQ in Relationships: Gottman's Discoveries.

hook.text: John Gottman can predict divorce with 93% accuracy — by watching a couple argue for just 15 minutes.

buildup.text: His 'Four Horsemen' — criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and stonewalling — are the communication patterns that predict divorce.

discovery.text: Contempt — expressing superiority and disgust — is the single strongest predictor of relationship failure.

twist.text: The antidote isn't grand gestures. It's small moments of 'turning toward' your partner's bids for emotional connection.

climax.text: Happy couples have a 5:1 ratio of positive to negative interactions. Unhappy ones dip below 1:1.

punchline.text: Love doesn't die from big betrayals. It dies from small moments of turning away.

quiz.question: What is the strongest predictor of relationship failure according to Gottman?

details.summary: John Gottman's research can predict relationship success with over 90 percent accuracy based on emotional interaction patterns. The Four Horsemen of relationship failure are criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and stonewalling. Their antidotes are all emotional intelligence skills.
details.whyItMatters: Gottman's research proves that relationship success is not about compatibility or luck but about learnable emotional skills applied consistently.
takeaways: Gottman predicts relationship success with over 90 percent accuracy
Four Horsemen: criticism, contempt, defensiveness, stonewalling
Their antidotes are all emotional intelligence skills

faq.question: What are the antidotes to Gottman's Four Horsemen?
faq.answer: For criticism, use gentle startup with I-statements. For contempt, build a culture of appreciation. For defensiveness, take responsibility for your part. For stonewalling, practice self-soothing and request breaks when overwhelmed. Each antidote is a specific emotional intelligence skill.

faq.question: Which of the Four Horsemen is most destructive?
faq.answer: Contempt. Gottman's research identifies contempt as the single strongest predictor of relationship failure. It communicates disgust and superiority, attacking the partner's sense of self. Contempt also correlates with the recipient's physical illness. Eliminating contempt is the highest priority.
